_comment: SELF-HOST variant of descriptors/ceos-lab-readonly-descriptor.json for the firewall-a3-partner-path use case: identical tools/schemas, endpoint = the rig running ON THE SAME HOST as your hub (127.0.0.1:3107). The hub admits it only when HUB_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST lists 127.0.0.1:3107 (docs/RUNNING.md → Registering a service on your own network). The pipeline's Harvester fetches this file from its raw GitHub URL and self-provisions the service (register → read-only calls → teardown).
name: ceos-lab-readonly
description: Read-only Arista EOS network-state harvest for the network-provisioning pipeline. Exposes list_devices, fetch_data (NAPALM getters: running-config, interfaces, facts, BGP neighbors, etc.), and show_commands restricted to an enumerated allowlist of state-read commands (route tables, OSPF/IS-IS neighbors, IS-IS hostname map) against a cEOS lab. Authenticates to devices with a static service credential (validation rig; not JWKS per-user identity). No preconditions; call fetch_data with getter names, or show_commands with allowlisted commands.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: List network devices and inventory (devices, groups, or both). Read-only. Call this first to discover device names before fetch_data.

details.description: Return full device attributes (for a devices query)

tools.name: fetch_data
tools.description: Execute one or more READ-ONLY NAPALM getters against the EOS devices and return structured state (running-config, interfaces, facts, BGP neighbors, etc.). This is the Phase-0 harvest surface. Read-only by construction — NAPALM getters never mutate device state.

getters.description: NAPALM getter names to run (short form, no 'get_' prefix). All entries are read-only EOS getters.

filter_name.description: Restrict to one inventory device name (e.g. 'ceos1')

tools.name: show_commands
tools.description: Execute READ-ONLY operational 'show' commands from the enumerated allowlist below and return raw CLI output. Added for route-table, IGP-adjacency and link-state-database state that NAPALM getters cannot retrieve (parity verification, neighbour baselines). NOTE on parity during protocol coexistence: while one IGP is administratively preferred, the other's routes are computed but NOT installed, so routing-table views show them as absent even on a healthy fabric — the link-state database is where that evidence lives. Commands outside the allowlist are not part of this service's declared surface — do not send them.

commands.description: Allowlisted read-only show commands to run on the filtered devices.

filter_name.description: Restrict to one inventory device name (e.g. 'ceos1')
